# City of God

## Identity and consulted witness

Augustine, City of God 18.9, trans. Marcus Dods, Logos Virtual Library digital witness. [Selected digital carrier](https://www.logoslibrary.org/augustine/city/1809.html). Accessed and saved 8 September 2026. The raw response is retained at `working/sources-texts-references/primary-texts/attica/augustine-city-god-dods-digital.html` (SHA-256 `d4f303830411b82af45172086826a1613b7eebaab22f2286199c8d2679f6fac4`). A saved page can contain more material than the selected reading; no whole-work reading is claimed.

## Source-specific reading

Augustine attributes the naming narrative to Varro. Olive and water prompt consultation of Delphi; the oracle leaves the choice to the citizens. Cecrops assembles both sexes, and the women’s majority of one secures Minerva’s name. Neptune devastates the land, and the account makes women lose the vote, maternal naming and the Athenian designation as appeasement.

Augustine’s argument then turns against the victorious goddess: she cannot protect those who made her victorious. His demonic interpretation is part of his theological polemic. The narrative attributed to Varro and Augustine’s use of it remain distinguishable. No separately recovered Varro text, or historical constitutional transition, has been admitted here.
